questions.q: Why does the lesson say a runbook with no real incidents in it is still theoretical?
options: Because runbooks are never useful
Because it covers detection, triage, containment, and communication only in the abstract, untested against anything real
Because it was written by the wrong person
Because Lesson 7's runbook has no detection phase at all
questions.explain: A worked example is what turns the runbook from a document into something a responder has seen actually used.

questions.q: What five parts structure the worked example Mara adds?
options: Detection, triage, root cause, remediation, validation
Scope, budget, timeline, stakeholders, sign-off
Alert, escalation, legal notice, press release, closure
Planning, ingestion, correlation, CA pilot, documentation
questions.explain: The worked example mirrors the runbook's own phases: detection, triage, root cause, remediation, and validation.

questions.q: What are the two concrete parts of the new standing control?
options: A per-change gate requiring documented justification and second-person review, plus a periodic review auditing existing rule scopes
A single annual meeting with no other process change
A general reminder to firewall administrators to be more careful
An automated tool that deletes any rule wider than a /24
questions.explain: The control has a per-change gate for future changes and a periodic review for gaps that already exist.

questions.q: Why would the per-change gate alone not have caught this specific incident?
options: Because the gate only applies to Linux servers
Because this rule was written before the gate existed
Because the gate requires no documentation at all
Because the vendor refused to provide a documented range
questions.explain: The gate only governs changes made after it exists -- it cannot retroactively catch an already-live misconfigured rule.

questions.q: Why would the periodic review alone not be sufficient either?
options: Because periodic reviews are never accurate
Because it is slower and would not stop a brand-new mistake from going live in the meantime
Because Renee refuses to approve periodic reviews
Because periodic reviews only check CA policies, not firewall rules
questions.explain: A recurring audit alone leaves a window between reviews where a new, similarly broad rule could go live unnoticed.
